indicators.flag: Rounded sum purchases at grocery stores and/or other retailers that sell gift cards and/or prepaid credit cards.
indicators.red_flag: Round-dollar gift-card / prepaid-card retail spend
indicators.rationale: Rounded-sum spend at grocery/retail MCCs that sell gift/prepaid cards is fully derivable from the bank's own card-transaction stream (merchant MCC plus rounded-amount test) and is not typically run as a standing signal.

build_logic.logic: Flag a customer with repeated rounded-sum card purchases at grocery/general retailers whose MCC indicates gift-card or prepaid-card sales, indicating stored-value accumulation rather than ordinary grocery spend.
build_logic.source: card-transaction ledger with merchant MCC tags
build_logic.route: Tier-2 alert → AML analyst review gate

indicators.flag: Atypical high-value purchases at convenience stores, particularly those that sell gift cards, prepaid credit cards,
indicators.red_flag: High-value convenience-store buys at gift-card / prepaid outlets
indicators.rationale: Atypically high-value purchases at convenience-store MCCs are derivable from the card stream by comparing transaction value against the expected spend distribution for that MCC, with no external attribution needed.

build_logic.logic: Flag customers whose convenience-store purchases are high-value outliers versus the typical convenience-store spend distribution, particularly at locations whose MCC indicates gift-card, prepaid-card, or money-transfer sales.
build_logic.source: card-transaction ledger with merchant MCC tags
build_logic.route: Tier-2 alert → AML analyst review gate

indicators.flag: Purchases at online merchants that specialize in selling gift cards.
indicators.red_flag: Online gift-card-vendor purchases
indicators.rationale: Purchases at gift-card online merchants are visible from card data, but online-gift-card MCCs already feed existing stored-value/AML spend controls, so this sharpens an existing control rather than a net-new build.

indicators.flag: Purchases and/or payments at luxury vehicle dealerships or for limousine services.
indicators.red_flag: Luxury-vehicle / limousine dealership spend
indicators.rationale: Luxury-vehicle/limousine payments are observable from transaction MCCs, but flagging them as anomalous needs KYC income/occupation context that is only partly structured, so an existing high-value-spend control can be enhanced.

indicators.flag: Purchases and/or payments at higher-end restaurants.
indicators.red_flag: High-end restaurant spend
indicators.rationale: Higher-end restaurant spend is observable from MCC data but is only meaningful against an expected-spend/lifestyle profile that is partially structured, so it enhances an existing lifestyle-anomaly control rather than standing alone.

indicators.flag: Purchases and/or payments at higher-end clothing, footwear, or accessories retailers.
indicators.red_flag: High-end apparel / footwear / accessories spend
indicators.rationale: High-end clothing/accessories spend is visible from MCCs but signifies money laundering only relative to expected-activity profile context that is partially structured, so it enhances an existing lifestyle-anomaly control.

indicators.red_flag: Cosmetic-surgery / enhancement-procedure spend
indicators.rationale: Cosmetic-surgery/medical-enhancement payments are observable from merchant data, but are only suggestive against a lifestyle/expected-activity profile that is partially structured, so they enhance an existing lifestyle-anomaly control.

indicators.flag: Purchases at higher-end nightclubs.
indicators.red_flag: High-end nightclub spend
indicators.rationale: Higher-end nightclub spend is visible from MCC data but is meaningful only against an expected-spend profile that is partially structured, so it enhances an existing lifestyle-anomaly control.

indicators.flag: Purchases at jewellery retailers.
indicators.red_flag: Jewellery-retailer spend
indicators.rationale: Jewellery-retailer purchases are observable from MCC data but indicate laundering only relative to an expected-activity profile that is partially structured, so they enhance an existing high-value-spend control.

indicators.flag: Frequent low-value payments for parking.
indicators.red_flag: High-frequency low-value parking payments
indicators.rationale: Frequent low-value parking payments are a concrete count/MCC pattern fully derivable from the card stream alone, and a parking-frequency signal is not typically instrumented.

build_logic.logic: Flag a customer with an unusually high frequency of low-value parking payments (by parking MCC) over the window, consistent with frequent short-stay venue visits rather than ordinary commuting.
build_logic.source: card-transaction ledger with merchant MCC tags
build_logic.route: Tier-2 alert → AML analyst review gate

indicators.red_flag: Frequent same-day food-delivery clustering
indicators.rationale: Multiple same-day food-delivery purchases are a count/timing pattern fully derivable from the card stream (food-delivery MCC plus same-day grouping), with no external data required.

build_logic.logic: Flag a customer with frequent food-delivery purchases that cluster multiple times on the same day, consistent with provisioning multiple people at one location rather than individual ordering.
build_logic.source: card-transaction ledger with merchant MCC tags
build_logic.route: Tier-2 alert → AML analyst review gate

indicators.flag: Purchases and/or payments to entities associated with jail collect calls.
indicators.red_flag: Payments to jail collect-call providers
indicators.rationale: Payments themselves are visible, but identifying the payee as a jail collect-call provider requires merchant-category/payee enrichment the bank holds only partially before the signal is reliable.

indicators.flag: Frequent transfers to virtual currency exchangers, particularly if these funds were sourced from incoming email
indicators.red_flag: VCE transfers funded by inbound e-transfers
indicators.rationale: Frequent transfers to virtual-currency exchangers funded by inbound EMTs from multiple individuals is a flow-through pattern fully derivable from the bank's own EMT and outbound-transfer records plus known-VCE counterparty tags.

build_logic.logic: Flag an account that makes frequent transfers to virtual-currency exchangers where the funding traces to incoming email money transfers from multiple distinct individuals, indicating collection-then-conversion layering.
build_logic.source: EMT records and outbound transfer ledger joined to known VCE counterparty tags

indicators.flag: Frequent transfers to individuals who conduct virtual currency exchanges on behalf of third parties, particularly
indicators.red_flag: Transfers to third-party VCE intermediaries
indicators.rationale: The transfer flow is observable from EMT data, but identifying the recipient as an informal VCE intermediary acting for third parties requires counterparty behaviour/attribution enrichment beyond core fields before the signal is reliable.

indicators.flag: Transfers to individuals or entities that advertise their virtual currency services on escort websites.
indicators.red_flag: Transfers to escort-site-advertised VCE services
indicators.rationale: Establishing that a transfer recipient advertises virtual-currency services on escort websites requires external open-source/web attribution the bank does not hold and must source before any signal is buildable.

indicators.flag: Frequent purchases and/or payments to online gambling/online casino platforms, particularly if these funds
indicators.red_flag: Frequent online-gambling / casino payments
indicators.rationale: Frequent payments to online-gambling/casino platforms funded by inbound EMTs are derivable from core data and already partly covered by existing gambling-velocity monitoring, so this sharpens an existing control.

indicators.flag: Frequent funds transferred to a reloadable prepaid credit card, particularly to multiple prepaid cards.
indicators.red_flag: Reloadable prepaid-card fan-out load pattern
indicators.rationale: Frequent loads to one or many reloadable prepaid cards is a count/destination pattern fully derivable from the bank's own transfer records and prepaid-card load data, and is not typically a standing signal.

build_logic.logic: Flag a customer who frequently transfers funds onto reloadable prepaid credit cards, especially across multiple distinct cards, indicating stored-value distribution consistent with layering.
build_logic.source: transfer ledger joined to prepaid-card load records
build_logic.route: Tier-2 alert → AML analyst review gate

indicators.flag: Female’s reloadable prepaid credit card is funded by reloads or transfers from a male, usually the same male.
indicators.red_flag: Prepaid-card reloads from a single male funder
indicators.rationale: The single-funder reload relationship is observable from transfer data, but the gender-role characterization relies on KYC gender attributes that are only partially reliable/structured, so the pattern needs enrichment before a signal.

indicators.flag: Excessive payments to multiple telephone or internet service providers.
indicators.red_flag: Payments to numerous distinct telecom / ISP payees
indicators.rationale: Excessive payments to multiple distinct telecom/ISP payees is a count/distinct-payee pattern fully derivable from the bank's own bill-payment and card data, and is not normally instrumented as a signal.

build_logic.logic: Flag a customer making excessive payments to an unusually high number of distinct telephone/internet service providers over the window, consistent with running multiple phone lines/ads rather than household use.
build_logic.source: bill-payment and card-transaction ledger with payee/MCC tags
build_logic.route: Tier-2 alert → AML analyst review gate

indicators.flag: Multiple phone numbers attempting to access a female’s bank account.
indicators.red_flag: Multi-phone-number access to one account
indicators.rationale: Channel/access metadata such as caller phone numbers is held by the bank only partially and outside the core transaction store, and the gender qualifier adds KYC dependency, so it needs enrichment before a reliable signal.

indicators.red_flag: Accommodation-booking / cash-deposit geo-coincidence
indicators.rationale: Correlating accommodation-booking locations with cash-deposit locations across multiple cities is derivable by joining the bank's own merchant/booking transactions and geotagged cash-deposit (ABM/branch) records it already holds.

build_logic.logic: Flag a customer whose accommodation-booking transaction locations coincide with their cash-deposit (ABM/branch) locations across multiple cities within the window, consistent with itinerant short-stay operation funded in cash.
build_logic.source: merchant transaction records (booking MCC) joined to geotagged ABM/branch cash-deposit records
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → AML analyst review gate

indicators.flag: Use of automatic banking machine(s) located in or near location(s) of accommodation booking(s), particularly if
indicators.red_flag: ABM cash use at/near accommodation-booking locations
indicators.rationale: Matching ABM-usage locations to accommodation-booking locations (and ordering them after the booking payment) is derivable from the bank's own geotagged ABM transactions and booking payments, no external data needed.

build_logic.logic: Flag a customer using ABMs in or near the location of an accommodation booking, particularly when the ABM activity follows the booking payment, consistent with cash handling at short-stay venues.
build_logic.source: geotagged ABM transaction records joined to booking-payment transactions
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → AML analyst review gate

indicators.red_flag: Frequent withdrawals at non-FI (white-label) ABMs

indicators.flag: Payments to online third party accommodations- or travel-booking websites.
indicators.red_flag: Online third-party travel / accommodation-booking spend
indicators.rationale: Payments to online travel/accommodation booking sites are visible from MCC data and already partly feed travel-spend monitoring, so this enhances an existing control rather than a net-new build.

indicators.flag: Transactions involving payment processors associated to escort websites or online gambling.
indicators.red_flag: Transactions via escort-site / gambling payment processors
indicators.rationale: Payment-processor transactions are visible, but attributing a processor to escort websites or online gambling requires processor/merchant attribution enrichment the bank holds only partially before the signal is reliable.

indicators.flag: Personal account received multiple funds transfers from payment processors.
indicators.red_flag: Personal account receiving payment-processor transfers
indicators.rationale: A personal (non-merchant) account receiving multiple inbound transfers from payment processors is fully derivable from the bank's own transfer records and account-type registry, and is atypical for a personal account so worth a standing signal.

build_logic.logic: Flag a personal-type account that receives multiple inbound funds transfers from payment processors over the window, behaviour expected of a merchant settlement account rather than a personal account.
build_logic.source: transfer ledger joined to account-type registry and processor counterparty tags

indicators.flag: Individual received numerous email money transfers with escort-related references from several parties, usually
indicators.red_flag: Multi-sender e-transfer fan-in with escort-related memos
indicators.rationale: The collect-then-redistribute EMT flow is observable from EMT records, but detecting 'escort-related references' depends on parsing free-text EMT memo fields that need enrichment before the signal is reliable.

indicators.red_flag: Inbound e-transfers memo-referencing an escort name
indicators.rationale: Inbound EMT counts are observable, but matching memo references to escort-agency names requires unstructured-memo parsing and a name list, so the pattern needs enrichment before a reliable signal.

indicators.rationale: Linking a customer's phone number to an escort agency requires external open-source/web attribution the bank does not natively hold, so this data must be sourced before any signal.

indicators.flag: Funds deposited to or withdrawn from a casino player’s gaming account with limited or no gambling involved.
indicators.red_flag: Casino gaming-account pass-through with no real play
indicators.rationale: Whether casino gaming-account deposits/withdrawals occurred 'with limited or no gambling' requires the casino operator's play data the bank does not hold; only the funds movement, not the gambling context, is observable internally.

indicators.flag: Funds deposited to or withdrawn from an investment account with limited or no purchases of investments.
indicators.red_flag: Investment-account pass-through with no real investing
indicators.rationale: For investment accounts the bank holds, deposits/withdrawals with little or no actual investment activity is fully derivable from its own investment subledger, and using the investment account as a pass-through is not typically instrumented.

build_logic.logic: Flag an investment account whose deposits and withdrawals are not matched by investment purchases over the window, indicating the account is used as a conduit rather than for genuine investing.
build_logic.source: investment-product subledger joined to account cash-flow records
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → AML analyst review gate

indicators.rationale: Frequent transfers to online investment entities are visible from the transfer ledger and already partly covered by velocity/outbound-transfer monitoring, so this sharpens an existing control.

indicators.red_flag: Business in a potential sexual-exploitation venue industry
indicators.rationale: Industry classification of a business customer is partly held via NAICS/business-type at onboarding, but reliably scoping the at-risk venue industries needs taxonomy enrichment, so the pattern needs enrichment before a signal.

indicators.flag: Use of separate accounts and/or separate credit cards to separate non-human trafficking related transactions
indicators.red_flag: Separate accounts / cards segregating transactions
indicators.rationale: Multiple accounts/cards per customer are visible, but distinguishing deliberate segregation of trafficking-related from other activity requires behavioural/contextual enrichment the bank holds only partially before a reliable signal.

indicators.flag: Incoming funds (cash deposits and incoming email money transfers) are immediately transferred to a business

indicators.rationale: Cash/EMT inflows immediately swept into a business account and then depleted by outbound EMTs and cash withdrawals is a funnel pass-through fully derivable from the bank's own transaction and account-type data.

build_logic.logic: Flag a business account that receives cash deposits and incoming EMTs which are promptly transferred in and then depleted by outgoing EMTs and cash withdrawals, indicating funnel-account layering rather than operating cash flow.
